events.title: Lua 5.0 released
events.summary: The [Lua] team released [Lua] 5.0 in April 2003 — a major rewrite with lexical scoping, metamethods, and coroutines.
events.about: [Lua] 5.0 is the dialect embedded in [Redis], World of Warcraft addons, [Nginx] (OpenResty), and game engines worldwide. Coroutines and metatables let hosts extend the language without bloating the core — the model for embedded scripting today.

narrative.whyChosen: [Lua] 5.0 is the version every modern embedding target still ships.
narrative.whyImportant: Lexical scoping and coroutines made [Lua] viable for serious game and server scripting.
narrative.problemSolved: [Lua] 4's dynamic scoping and limited coroutines restricted complex embedded logic.

events.title: AMD Opteron — first x86-64 CPU — launched
events.summary: AMD launched the Opteron processor on April 22, 2003 — the first [x86] [CPU] shipping with 64-bit AMD64 extensions (the ISA had been publicly documented since August 2000).
events.about: AMD64 extended 32-bit [x86] with 64-bit registers and larger address spaces while keeping backward compatibility — Intel followed with EM64T. Linux, Windows, and [macOS] adopted [x86]-64 as the default server and desktop architecture. Every modern cloud VM, [Docker] host, and backend binary still targets this ISA.

narrative.whyChosen: AMD64 broke the 4 GB memory wall without abandoning the [x86] software ecosystem.
narrative.whyImportant: It became the universal 64-bit architecture for servers, desktops, and developer machines.
narrative.problemSolved: 32-bit [x86] could not address enough [RAM] for large databases, [JVM] heaps, and in-memory analytics.
